## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-scheduled integration+decision kernel materializing a 1-byte death mask, with a host-side mask scan for respawn, can leverage Halide's auto-vectorization to outperform naive scalar on AoS layouts.

## Layout & approach
The 69 B/particle AoS struct offers 41% hot bytes in loop 1 (28 of 68 B: age+pos+vel), 5% in loop 2 (4 of 68 B: seed), 41% in loop 3 (28 of 68 B: color+pos); the rest is dead weight. The mask intermediate adds 1 B/particle. The approach delegates loop 1 to an opaque Halide call (`halide_b6_mask`) expected to vectorize, then host-scans the mask for respawn, then renders scalar. With L1d spill at N≈474, all measured points are L3-resident or DRAM.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across the two L3-resident points (N=10000–100000) — 24.9→24.1 ns/p at q=0.01, 27.6→28.0 at q=0.25. The L3→DRAM transition (N=100000→1000000) produces a modest 9–20% rise (24.1→26.8 at q=0.01, 26.0→31.3 at q=0.1), muted because the algo is frontend-bound (63–71% frontend stalls). Backend stalls climb from 0.1% in L3 to 8–16% in DRAM at q≥0.1, reflecting the respawn scan's random mask access, but never dominate. The knee is shallow — code bloat, not cache depth, sets cost.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.0–2.86 GB/s is 16–23% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling and 4.5–6.3x above the 5.437 ns/p memory floor — overwhelmingly frontend/overhead-bound. Against naive scalar it is essentially tied: 0.86–1.14x across all points. Against the winner (AF02.LP1-autovec.LP2-opt) it is 1.7–3.2x slower everywhere, widening as death rate drops: 3.2x slower at q=0.01 but 1.7x at q=0.5, because the winner's vectorized advantage is largest when few particles die.

## Assembly
Zero vector-suffixed instructions. The Halide kernel is an opaque `call halide_b6_mask` with no visible vectorization. Loop 1 math is scalar SSE (`vmovss`, `vmulss`, `vaddss`, `vucomiss`). The respawn scan is a 32-byte unrolled chain: `vmovdqu`+`vptest` to skip empty chunks, then 32× `cmp`/`je`/`call`, each preceded by `vzeroupper` (34 total). The render loop does byte-granular RMW via `movzx`/`add`/`cmovae`/`mov BYTE PTR`. The 629-instruction body with 34 `vzeroupper` barriers drives the 63–71% frontend stalls.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.86–1.14x of naive scalar (essentially tied) and 1.7–3.2x slower than the winner at every N×q point. The Halide kernel produced no vectorization (0 vector-suffixed instructions), the respawn scan is a 629-instruction unrolled branch chain with 34 `vzeroupper` barriers, and frontend stalls (63–71%) from code bloat — not memory bandwidth (16–23% of ceiling) — set the cost floor. The 1 B/particle mask adds write traffic for zero benefit.
